title: Warm Spicy Argentinian Duck Empanadas
description: A Jain-friendly Argentinian dish featuring duck sauce and double-rise bread, perfect for a midnight craving. These empanadas are filled with a jammy and bouncy duck filling.

ingredients.name: all purpose flour
ingredients.notes: for the double rise bread dough

ingredients.name: active dry yeast
ingredients.notes: for the double rise bread dough

instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine the flour, yeast, and a pinch of salt to make the double rise bread dough.
Gradually add warm water to the dry ingredients and knead the dough for 10 minutes until it becomes smooth and elastic.
Let the dough rise in a warm place for 1 hour, or until it has doubled in size.
Preheat the oven to 400 degrees Fahrenheit.
In a large pan, heat the vegetable oil over medium heat and saute the chopped onion and minced garlic until they are softened.
Add the duck sauce, cumin, paprika, salt, and black pepper to the pan and stir well to combine.
Punch down the risen dough and divide it into 8 equal pieces.
Roll out each piece of dough into a thin circle and place a tablespoon of the duck filling in the center of each circle.
Fold the dough over the filling to form a half moon shape and press the edges together to seal the empanada.
Brush the tops of the empanadas with a little water and bake them in the preheated oven for 20 minutes, or until they are golden brown.
Ensure poultry is cooked to an internal temperature of 74°C / 165°F (juices run clear, no pink remaining) before serving.
